messages.instruction_excerpt: Extract the product's stated properties from this submittal. Use these property names and meanings where they apply: {"cri": "Color quality (CRI)", "dim_min_percent": "Dims down to", "dlc_listed": "DLC listing", "document_revision": "Data sheet version", "efficacy_lm_per_w": "Efficiency (lumens per watt)", "f_rating_hr": "Fire rating (F)", "input_watts_120v": "Power at 120 V", "input_watts_277v": "Power at 277 V", "l70_hours": "Rated life (L70)", "lumens": "Light output", "macadam_steps": "macadam steps", "max_annular_space_in": "Largest gap it can seal", "penetrant_types": "Pipe types covered", "service_temp_max_f": "Highest service temperature", "service_temp_range_f": "Service temperature range", "standards": "Test standards", "t_rating_hr": "Temperature rating (T)", "voc_g_per_l": "VOC (air quality)", "warranty_years": "Warranty", "watts": "Power draw"}. Read every supplied page, including tables and notes. For a listed system, record its system number as model. Keep each test/rating metric distinct; never relabel a different metric to fit a requested name. Do not dump option tables. Omit SKU-dependent table values unless an exact submitted SKU is identified. A blank catalog-number field or an ordering example is not a submitted SKU selection. For other stated alternatives, retain distinct values without repeating the same value for every option. Set variant to the exact quoted option/configuration phrase whenever a value is limited to that option. Record the page and a short supporting quote for each claim, and the revision or date printed on the data sheet. Copy each quote verbatim as one contiguous substring from that page; never paraphrase or join separate passages. Omit properties that are not stated instead of returning null claims. For lists, put each distinct standard or certification identifier in its own array entry. For covered pipe types, quote the enumerated penetrating-item list, not the wall studs or sleeves.
